title: P0 HostedAPI - Region ringbuffer overflow causing partial 5xx and degraded streaming
content:
Summary:

On 2028-01-14 21:12 UTC we observed a multi-minute surge of 500/502 errors and increased streaming latency impacting ~12% of active sessions for the hosted API in eu-west-2. Impact lasted ~14 minutes with a small tail of degraded streaming frames for an additional 9 minutes. No customer data was exposed; errors were internal 5xx and timeouts. This was declared a P0 due to user-facing error surface and observable SLA impact.

High-level impact:
- 12% of streaming sessions in eu-west-2 experienced partial failures (stalled chunks, reconnects).
- Non-streaming generation endpoints in the region saw increased tail latency and ~2.6% 5xx rate spike.
- Cross-region failover (latency-based) automatically diverted a small fraction of traffic to eu-central-1; majority remained in eu-west-2.

Detection and timeline (UTC):
- 21:11:30 - Synthetic canaries (streaming) show first frame delay rising above SLO (95th > 1.8s). Pager triggered.
- 21:12:05 - Oncall sees streaming consumer errors and elevated 502 counts in region dashboard.
- 21:13:00 - SREs correlate 502s with a single pool of edge-serving workers behind the regional ingress.
- 21:14:40 - Log sampling shows connection pool draining and repeated RingBufferOverflow exceptions from the serving-runtime (edge sidecar).
- 21:17:00 - Mitigation: traffic weighted away from pool and region autoscaler increased replica count. 502 rate begins to subside.
- 21:25:00 - Primary mitigation complete; services stable but with residual client reconnects.
- 21:34:00 - All routes back to baseline; incident moved to postmortem work.

Immediate mitigation steps taken:
1) Rotated regional ingress to healthy worker subset (took ~3 min to reconfigure and warm).
2) Temporarily increased edge pool size and reduced per-worker concurrency by 30% (to reduce per-process memory pressure).
3) Enabled aggressive request shedding for non-auth traffic at the ingress to prioritize active streaming sessions.
4) Scoped emergency hotfix to serving-runtime config to increase ringbuffer capacity on the sidecar (deployed as a canary to 10% then rolled to 100% for the pool).

Root cause analysis (initial):
- The root cause was an unanticipated ring buffer growth pattern in the streaming sidecar under a specific traffic burst shape. A sequence of short-lived spikes with high fanout (many simultaneous session starts + rapid small messages) triggered an internal ringbuffer enqueue path that had a rare race where consumers paused briefly due to GC + scheduler jitter, causing producers to temporarily exceed capacity. The overflow path throws RingBufferOverflow exceptions which were not being backpressured correctly at the ingress, causing upstream requests to fail with 502/500.
- A contributing factor was a recent optimization (serving-runtime PR #4067) that increased per-worker batching concurrency and reduced polling frequency for the consumer thread to decrease CPU usage. Under normal load this saved CPU, but it widened the window where a paused consumer would allow producers to push more items, increasing transient occupancy and exposing the ringbuffer overflow.
- Autoscaler backoff and slow reaction time for the specific pool topology made the condition last longer than ideal (we had a 45s scale-up cool-off in that pool).

Why did this produce client-visible 5xx?
- The sidecar overflow bubbled up to the ingress via an error path that didn't map overflow -> 429 (reject) but instead aborted requests to upstream with a 500/502. In other words we failed closed instead of failing fast/returning short-circuit rejects.

Logs and metrics supporting RCA: (summary lines, full traces in linked_artifacts) - Repeated logs: "RingBufferOverflow[streaming-sidecar] producer=conn-... consumer-paused=true backlog=xxxx" - CPU/GC spike for sidecar instances correlated with the burst window - Increased per-worker queue lengths immediately preceding overflows

Why wasn't existing runbook sufficient?
- Current streaming-runbook assumed ringbuffer overflows were extremely rare and recommended immediate restart of the sidecar. Restarting individual sidecars without addressing the ingress policy led to cascading reconnects and did not stop new producers from hitting overflow until we reduced concurrency at ingress. The runbook also lacked a clear guidance to change the mapping of overflow -> HTTP reject code.

Post-incident follow-ups (short-term, P0-P1 hygiene):
1) Change overflow semantics in the sidecar: map RingBufferOverflow to a non-fatal reject path that returns 429 to the client and signals upstream to retry (owner: serving-runtime, PR tracked: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/4188, due 2028-01-22).
2) Revert the consumer polling reduction from PR #4067 for streaming sidecars in eu regions until we can validate under synthetic stress (owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime, opt-in canary 2028-01-20).
3) Reduce autoscaler cool-off time for edge-serving pools with high session churn from 45s -> 10s (owner: infra/autoscaler, due 2028-01-21).
4) Add an ingress-level short-circuit that turns sidecar overflow into 429s and triggers exponential backoff on clients (owner: edge-team, due 2028-01-23).
5) Add targeted synthetic load test (session start fanout + tiny message bursts) to CI to validate ringbuffer behavior and consumer backpressure (owner: sres + qa, test added by 2028-01-28).

Longer-term action items (design/architecture):
- Explore moving to a bounded backpressure-aware enqueue API that blocks/pauses producers rather than dropping/throwing at the point of enqueue. This is a larger change touching SDKs and ingress semantics; start feasibility study Q2 2028 (owner: serving-runtime arch).
- Revisit batching-concurrency optimization across all regions with a safety net that disables the optimization if GC pause patterns exceed threshold (owner: apml/serving-runtime research).
- Consider a regional quota token bucket to limit session start rate per minute per region during high churn events to avoid local storms. (owner: platform-engineering).

Runbook draft (quick playbook for SRE when RingBufferOverflow alerts spike):
- Pager -> rotate to oncall SRE and edge lead.
- Immediate steps (first 5 minutes):
  1) Verify Canary and region metrics. Confirm ringbuffer overflow logs exist.
  2) If >3 sidecars show overflow: reduce ingress concurrency target for the pool to 50% of normal (via runtime config toggle).
  3) Enable ingress short-circuit to return 429 for known overflow signatures (toggle location: edge-config/service-overflow-policy).
  4) If errors persist beyond 3 mins, ramp pool replicas + reweight traffic away from affected AZs/POPs.
  5) Avoid mass restarting sidecars unless you have ingress short-circuit enabled (restart can cause reconnection storms).

- Follow-up (post-stable):
  1) Capture heap/GC traces for sidecars that overflowed.
  2) Tag traces and tracesets with request patterns and attach to the incident ticket.
  3) Prepare a small repro and run in staging; iterate on consumer polling interval.

Customer communication notes (what went out / what to do):
- At T+20m we posted an incident status to status.redwood.com indicating "Partial degraded streaming in eu-west-2; engineers investigating; mitigation in progress."
- We will follow up with an RCA email to affected customers highlighting corrective action items and mitigation (owner: customer-success, draft due 2028-01-20).

Postmortem owner + next steps:
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) - overall RCA and runbook update.
- Serving-runtime owner: Ben Cho - patching overflow semantics and PRs to revert the consumer polling change.
- Edge/Ingress owner: Jacob Kim - implement short-circuit mapping and ingress policy changes.
- Autoscaler owner: Renee Martin - modify cool-off tuning for high-churn pools.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only eu-west-2 surface this issue and not other eu regions with similar runtime versions? Hypothesis: subtle workload shape + multi-tenant traffic correlated with a job in that region (investigating background batch jobs and partner traffic).
- Exact probability of overflow under new synthetic load; need quantification for SLO tuning.

Appendix - useful snippets:
- Representative log message: "RingBufferOverflow sidecar=stream-abc producer_conn=... backlog=13248 consumer_paused_ms=72"
- KQL query used: logs | where message contains "RingBufferOverflow" | summarize count() by sidecar, bin(timestamp, 1m)
- Slack channel: #sre-incident-8572 (link in linked_artifacts)

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- We gained a lot from the short-circuit idea; that should be a standard primitive for any overflow/pressure condition (a formal API between sidecar and ingress).
- Need to be careful with restarting strategies; mass restarts are dangerous without ingress-level shedding.
- Follow-on: coordinate a synthetic "start storm" test with platform + QA on 2028-01-25 to validate fixes before rolling region-wide.

Document history:
- 2028-01-15: initial incident notes and timeline (Aisha)
- 2028-01-16: added mitigation steps and early RCA (Ben, Jacob)
- 2028-01-19: finalized short-term action list, runbook draft, and owners assigned (Aisha).

If anything in this doc conflicts with linked artifacts, follow the canonical JIRA ticket (JIRA-8572) for the latest action items.
